questions.question: What's the main advantage of the Options pattern (`IOptions<NotifierSettings>`) over raw `builder.Configuration["Notifier:FromAddress"]` string access?
options: Strongly-typed access with IntelliSense — a typo'd config key silently leaves a default value rather than being caught, but at least the C# property name itself can't be mistyped without a compile error
The Options pattern is faster at runtime
Raw string access doesn't work at all in ASP.NET Core
questions.explanation: Binding configuration to a real class lets you write `_settings.FromAddress` with compiler-checked property names and autocomplete, instead of scattering string literal keys (each a typo risk) throughout your codebase.

questions.question: What's the difference between `_logger.LogInformation("Sending to " + to)` and `_logger.LogInformation("Sending to {To}", to)`?
options: No difference — both just produce text
The second keeps 'To' as a separate, named, structured field a logging provider (like Serilog) can capture and query independently — not just baked into a flat string
questions.explanation: This is structured logging's whole point: `{To}` is a named placeholder the logging framework tracks as its own field (queryable, filterable in log tools), unlike string concatenation which produces only an opaque block of text.

questions.question: Why should application code depend on `ILogger<T>` rather than directly calling Serilog's API?
options: It's the same Dependency Inversion idea from Module 2 — code depends on the logging ABSTRACTION, so the concrete provider (Serilog, or anything else) can be swapped or reconfigured without touching application code
Serilog doesn't have its own API
There's no real reason, it's just convention
questions.explanation: Exactly like INotifier/IStudentRepository earlier in the course — depending on ILogger<T> means the actual logging destination(s) and format are a configuration/wiring concern, not something scattered through business logic.

questions.question: What does `builder.Services.Configure<NotifierSettings>(builder.Configuration.GetSection("Notifier"))` do?
options: Binds the "Notifier" section of appsettings.json to a NotifierSettings instance, made available for injection as IOptions<NotifierSettings>
questions.explanation: This registers the binding: whatever JSON is under the "Notifier" key gets mapped onto NotifierSettings' properties, and any class can then receive it via constructor-injected IOptions<NotifierSettings>.

questions.question: Once Serilog is configured in Program.cs to write structured JSON logs to a file, every `_logger.LogInformation(...)` call throughout the app automatically benefits, with no changes to that calling code.
questions.explanation: This is the payoff of coding against ILogger<T>: the logging destination/format is entirely a Program.cs configuration concern. Code that just calls _logger.LogInformation(...) never needs to know or care that Serilog is writing JSON to a file underneath.
